report.title: Vault Security Review
report.subject: src/Vault.sol
report.methodology: Manual line-by-line review, property enumeration, rounding-direction analysis, and adversarial scenario modelling against an interest-bearing, over-collateralised single-asset lending vault.
report.note: This is an illustrative audit report produced for the Guardian Pipeline. It demonstrates how a static, point-in-time review (the artifact Landsman et al. 2025 found weakly correlated with exploit prevention) is converted into continuous, multi-layered assurance (Bourveau et al. 2024) by binding every security-relevant finding to a fuzz-harness invariant, a live monitor, and an exploit replay.

findings.title: Demo insolvency backdoor isolated to a separate contract
findings.description: An earlier revision shipped a privileged attack() function inside src/Vault.sol that forced the vault insolvent for the live-detection demo. Auditing a contract that contains its own backdoor is unsound. Remediation: attack() has been removed from Vault entirely and now lives only in src/AttackableVault.sol, a demo-only subclass that is never deployed to production. The audited Vault carries no privileged accounting path of any kind.
findings.recommendation: Resolved. Keep the demo breach confined to AttackableVault and deploy only src/Vault.sol to production. AttackableVault additionally reverts attack() on Base mainnet as defence-in-depth.

continuousAssurance.rationale: INV-01 is fuzz-proven against Vault pre-deploy and monitored every block post-deploy. EXP-01 replays the AttackableVault breach to prove the live layer still catches an insolvency regardless of its cause.

findings.title: Reentrancy exposure on state-mutating functions
findings.description: deposit, withdraw, borrow, repay and liquidate move ERC-20 value. A token with transfer hooks (ERC-777-style) would otherwise open a reentrancy surface against the liquidity and collateral checks. Remediation: the contract inherits OpenZeppelin's ReentrancyGuard and all five mutating functions are marked nonReentrant.
findings.recommendation: Resolved — retain the ReentrancyGuard. The fuzz harness exercises a non-callback MockERC20 and cannot reproduce a reentrant sequence, so INV-01 remains the continuous safety net for this class rather than the harness.

continuousAssurance.rationale: The ReentrancyGuard blocks this class structurally, but the harness exercises a non-callback MockERC20 and cannot reproduce a reentrant call sequence — so the finding is not proven absent by the harness. It is monitored live: any reentrancy that drained value would break INV-01 and alert within one block. The traceability map surfaces this as monitored-only — a deliberately partial-coverage finding.

findings.title: Full-close repayment could erode the solvency margin by one wei
findings.description: An earlier revision of _burnDebt charged a full repayment the borrower's nominal userDebt(). Because totalBorrowed() floors totalBorrowShares * borrowIndex, removing a borrower's shares can drop the floored aggregate by one wei more than the nominal debt — so the vault collected one wei less than debt actually fell, eroding the solvency margin. The invariant fuzz harness found this within a few hundred runs (a shrunk deposit/borrow/repay sequence). Remediation: a full close now charges the realised drop in totalBorrowed(), so cash rises by exactly what debt falls by.
findings.recommendation: Resolved. The realised-drop accounting keeps INV-01 exact; the invariant campaign now runs with zero solvency violations across 300,000+ calls.

continuousAssurance.rationale: This finding was surfaced by the harness itself — the pre-deployment layer working as designed. INV-01 is the property it violated; it is now both fuzz-proven and monitored live so any reintroduction is caught on both sides of deployment.

findings.title: Liquidation seizing all collateral must clear the full debt
findings.description: liquidate seizes collateral worth the repaid amount plus the liquidation bonus. Without a guard, a partial repayment could seize a borrower's entire share balance while leaving debt outstanding — an account with zero collateral but non-zero debt, i.e. unrecoverable bad debt. Remediation: when the seizure would consume all of the borrower's shares, liquidate reverts with MustClearDebt unless the liquidator is closing the full position.
findings.recommendation: Resolved. The MustClearDebt guard makes INV-06 (no uncollateralised debt) hold by construction.

continuousAssurance.rationale: INV-06 asserts a zero-collateral account holds no debt. The harness fuzzes liquidation alongside interest accrual; EXP-06 replays the interest-driven liquidation path end to end. Both confirm the guard holds.

findings.title: Sustained interest can make a lender redemption exceed idle cash
findings.description: withdraw pays out shares * totalSupplyAssets / totalSupplyShares and reverts with InsufficientLiquidity if idle cash cannot cover it. Once interest has lifted a lender's claim above the un-borrowed cash, a full redemption reverts until borrowers repay. This is correct behaviour for a lending vault, but a caller may be surprised; the revert is graceful and corrupts no state.
findings.recommendation: Acknowledged. Document that lender redemptions are bounded by available liquidity, as in any lending market. No code change required — the revert is the intended outcome.

continuousAssurance.rationale: The liquidity revert protects INV-01: the vault never pays out assets it does not hold. EXP-04 confirms the buffer survives a maximal borrow, and INV-01 holds the line in the harness and live.

findings.title: Share price is immune to direct token donations
findings.description: Anyone can transfer the asset directly to the vault, raising token.balanceOf(vault). Because sharePrice is derived from the stored totalSupplyAssets — not the token balance — a donation cannot move the shares-to-assets ratio. This structurally prevents the ERC-4626 first-depositor inflation attack; the donated funds simply enlarge the solvency margin.
findings.recommendation: Acknowledged. No change required — the stored-assets accounting model is the mitigation. Monitors must treat cash >= claims as a >= relation, not equality.

continuousAssurance.rationale: INV-04 (share price >= 1:1) and INV-01 (solvency) bound the lender side. EXP-02 replays the donation/inflation class and confirms the victim is not diluted.

findings.title: A full-close repayment may charge up to one wei above userDebt()
findings.description: Closing a position charges the realised drop in floored totalBorrowed(), which equals userDebt() or, by one wei of index rounding, one wei more. A caller repaying exactly userDebt() may therefore transfer one extra wei. This is the deliberate fix for GUA-03 — charging the realised cost is what keeps solvency exact.
findings.recommendation: Acknowledged. Document that callers should approve a small surplus when closing a position, as is standard for index-based debt. The one-wei direction always favours the protocol.

continuousAssurance.rationale: The one-wei overshoot exists precisely to keep INV-01 exact. The harness proves the rounding direction never erodes the solvency margin across the full invariant campaign.

findings.title: Deeply under-water positions can leave residual bad debt
findings.description: If interest pushes a borrower's debt above the full value of their collateral, no rational liquidator will repay it — closing the position would cost more than the collateral seized. The position then retains both shares and debt indefinitely. The 80% collateral cap and 5% liquidation bonus incentivise liquidation well before this point, but an idle, deeply under-water position is not structurally prevented.
findings.recommendation: Acknowledged. For a production deployment, add a reserve factor and a bad-debt socialisation path. The debt remains counted in totalBorrowed, so INV-01 stays well-defined; the residual risk is economic, not an accounting break.

continuousAssurance.rationale: Residual bad debt does not break INV-01 — the debt is still counted as an asset — but the live monitor tracks the solvency margin so erosion is visible. EXP-06 exercises the interest-driven liquidation path that keeps healthy positions cleared.
